result.summary: Re-derived the classification-field construction independently from the doc's exact wording (lib/letflow/design/iss0703-oidc-verifier-exception-handling.md, S3/S3a). (1) Structurally leak-proof: rescue branch uses `exception.__struct__` -- a compile-time-constant atom naming the exception's defstruct module, which cannot be forged/derived from a raised struct's field content under any circumstance; this is a hard language-level guarantee, not an assumption. catch branch: non-atom `reason` maps to one of two literal fixed constant atoms (:non_atom_exit_reason / :non_atom_throw_reason) -- also hard-safe. catch branch's third case, `is_atom(reason) -> classification = reason`, is NOT a formatter (confirmed: no Exception.message/1, inspect/1, to_string/1, or interpolation appears anywhere in S3/S3a's construction rules) and satisfies the AC's literal 'no formatter ever applied' test. Noting one non-blocking observation for the record: the doc's own justification for that branch ('atoms are drawn from the BEAM's fixed atom table, not built at runtime from arbitrary binary content') overstates the guarantee -- Elixir/Erlang atoms CAN in principle be constructed at runtime from arbitrary binary content (String.to_atom/1, :erlang.binary_to_atom/2), so in a hypothetical where an oidcc/jose dependency itself exits/throws a dynamically-token-derived atom, that atom's content would pass through as classification verbatim (not a construction defect in this design -- this code never builds such an atom itself, it would only be passing through an already-malicious upstream value). This is not a realistic path for oidcc/jose (dynamic atom creation from request-derived binary content is avoided in idiomatic BEAM library code precisely because of atom-table-exhaustion risk, and observed oidcc/jose exit/throw reasons are fixed literal atoms), and per (2) below TEST-DESIGNER's required non-leakage assertion is a mechanism-agnostic runtime check on the actual returned/logged values, so it would catch this hypothetical too if it ever materialized. Does not block PASS. (2) TEST-DESIGNER guidance (S7) requires an explicit non-leakage assertion: refute the returned classification (and the captured Logger.warning output via ExUnit.CaptureLog) contains any substring of length >= 4 of the fixture raw_token, or equivalently assert classification is a member of the small fixed enumerated set -- confirmed present and explicit, satisfies SECURITY-REVIEWER's BLOCKER recommendation. (3) All 6 of step-02's original ACs re-confirmed against the current doc: boundary + exact tuple shape (S2, S3) -- present; both oidcc calls covered in one boundary (S2) -- present; corrected moduledoc text (S6) -- present; TEST-DESIGNER guidance naming the real adapter, non-JWT-shaped token, fail-then-pass (S7) -- present; no .ex implementation-code bodies -- the only fenced blocks are the @type crash_reason line, an unmodified quote of existing auth_pipeline.ex code (already cleared in iteration 1), and the @spec/def-head signature with no body -- consistent with iteration 1's fix, no rescue/catch/def bodies anywhere; no auth_pipeline.ex change proposed, explicit statement in S3a -- present. (4) No new implementation-code-shaped fenced blocks introduced by this revision -- the only fenced-block edit is the field rename (message->classification) inside the pre-existing @type line; no new code blocks added.
